# 11QMelchizedek Column 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q13 (Cave 11), Col. 2 | **Condition:** fragmentary; main surviving column with ~26 partially preserved lines

---

**2:1** [...and concerning what] He said: "In [this] year-of-the-jubilee, [each-one-of-you shall return to-his-property" (Lev 25:13);

**2:2** and concerning what] He said: "Eve[ry] possessor-of-a-loan-of his-hand shall release [what he has lent to-his-neighbor; he shall not exact-it-of his-neighbor and-his-brother, for]

**2:3** the release of-God [has been proclaimed]" (Deut 15:2).

**2:4** [Its inter]pretation for-the-last-days concerns the-captives, about whom

**2:5** He said: "To proclaim liberty to-the-captives" (Isa 61:1). Its interpretation: He will assign them to-the-Sons-of-Heaven and to-the-inheritance-of-Melchizedek,

**2:6** [for He will re]store them. And he will proclaim to-them liberty, to-release-them from [the-debt-of] all their-iniquities.

**2:7** And this will [happen] in-the-first week-of-the-jubilee that-follows the-ni[ne] jubilees.

**2:8** And the-Day-of-[Atone]ment is the-e[nd-of-the] tenth [jub]ilee,

**2:9** when atonement-shall-be-made for-all the-Sons-of-[Light and] for-the-men-of the-lot-of-Mel[chi]zedek.

**2:10** [...over the]m [...] according-to [...] for

**2:11** that is the-time-of "the-year-of-favor" for-Melchizedek (Isa 61:2), and [of-his] arm[ies,

**2:12** the-nati]on-of the-holy-ones-of-God, of-the-rule-of judgment, as it-is-written

**2:13** concerning-him in-the-songs-of-David, who said: "Elohim stands in-the-as[sembly-of-God];

**2:14** in-the-midst-of the-gods he-judges" (Ps 82:1). And concerning-him he said: "[Let-the-assembly-of the-peoples]

**2:15** return above-it; and-on-high God will-[j]udge the-peoples" (Ps 7:8–9).

**2:16** As-for what he-sa[id: "How-long will-you] judge unjustly and-sh[ow]

**2:17** partiality to-the-wicked? [Se]lah" (Ps 82:2).

**2:18** Its interpretation concerns Belial and-the-spirits-of-his-lot, who [...]

**2:19** in-their-tur[ning]-away from-the-commandments-of-God [to-commit-evil].

**2:20** And Melchizedek will-exact the-veng[eance]-of the-judgments-of-God [from-the-hand-of-Be]lial and-from-the-hand-of all-the-[spirits-of]-his-[lot].

**2:21** And all the-[eternal] gods are-for-his-help. [This] is-what [He-said]:

**2:22** all the-sons-of-Mi[ght and ...] the-[a]ffair-of-Melchizedek.

**2:23** And [concerning-what He-said]: "How-beautiful upon-the-mountains are-the-feet-of the-messen[ger who]

**2:24** proclaims peace, the-messen[ger-of-good who-proclaims-salva]tion, who-says to-Zion: 'Your-God [reigns]'" (Isa 52:7).

**2:25** Its interpretation: the-mountains are the-pro[phets ...] the-messenger is the-anoin[ted-of-the-Spir]it,

**2:26** about-whom Dan[iel] said: ["Until an-anointed-one, a-prince" (Dan 9:25) ...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 2 of 11Q13 is the primary surviving text of the Melchizedek Scroll. The Hebrew employs pesher-style exegesis, citing and interpreting biblical texts (Lev 25:13, Deut 15:2, Isa 52:7, 61:1–2, Ps 82:1–2, Ps 7:8–9, Dan 9:25). Melchizedek is presented as a heavenly, eschatological figure — not merely the priest-king of Genesis 14 — who executes divine judgment against Belial at the end of the tenth jubilee. "Elohim" in Ps 82:1 is applied directly to Melchizedek, identifying him with a divine judge in the heavenly council. Construct chains hyphenated throughout to preserve Hebrew syntax. Lacunae marked with [...] represent genuine manuscript damage; reconstructed text in brackets follows standard scholarly restorations (Kobelski, van der Woude, Puech). "Sons of Heaven" (bene shamayim) and "Sons of Light" (bene 'or) are Qumran sectarian designations preserved literally.*
